definitions.explanation: Reluctant to spend money, even in situations where spending would be normal or expected.
Engaging in petty behavior to gain small advantages, often in ways that are seen as underhanded or beneath one's dignity.

examples.japanese: せこいことを{言|い}うな。
{彼|かれ}はせこいから{割|わ}り{勘|かん}でも1{円|えん}{単位|たんい}まで{計算|けいさん}する。
examples.english: He's so stingy that even when splitting the bill, he calculates down to the last yen.

examples.japanese: せこい{手段|しゅだん}で{勝|か}っても{嬉|うれ}しくない。
examples.english: Winning through petty means doesn't make me happy.

examples.japanese: そんなせこいこと{言|い}わないでよ。
examples.english: Don't be so petty about it.

examples.japanese: ポイントを{少|すこ}しでも{多|おお}くもらおうと、せこい{買|か}い{方|かた}をしてしまう。
examples.english: I end up shopping in petty ways to get even a few more reward points.

notes:
FORMS:
・せこい (plain)
・せこく (adverbial)
・せこさ (noun) - stinginess, pettiness

REGISTER:
Informal/colloquial. Can be mildly insulting when used to describe someone directly.

SIMILAR WORDS:
・けち - stingy, miserly (stronger criticism)
・{貧乏|びんぼう}くさい - looking poor, cheap
・こすい - cunning, crafty (regional/colloquial)
・みみっちい - petty, stingy

CONTRAST:
・{気前|きまえ}がいい - generous
・{太|ふと}っ{腹|ぱら} - generous, big-hearted

USAGE NOTES:
Originally from Kansai dialect but now widely used throughout Japan. Often used to criticize not just financial stinginess but also petty behavior in general.
